s1.syndrome_frame: A middle-aged woman with a parotid gland mass and subsequent development of systemic symptoms including facial swelling, abdominal bloating, easy bruising, and significant weight gain, with a time course of 18 months
salient_findings: Facial swelling, abdominal bloating, easy bruising, and significant weight gain
Elevated serum cortisol and ACTH levels
key_facts: 52-year-old woman presented with a mass on her left parotid gland
Initial presentation did not include constitutional symptoms
Developed facial swelling, abdominal bloating, easy bruising, and 30-lb weight gain 18 months after initial presentation
Blood pressure elevated from 120/78 mm Hg to 193/113 mm Hg
Imaging showed a 2.4-cm parotid mass and a 2.7-cm level IIB lymph node
Fine-needle aspiration biopsy showed features of a salivary gland neoplasm with atypia

s4.champion: Cushing's syndrome due to ectopic ACTH-producing tumor

raw.champion: Cushing's syndrome due to ectopic ACTH-producing tumor
raw.rationale: The patient's elevated serum cortisol, ACTH level, random blood glucose, and midnight salivary cortisol, along with the presence of a parotid gland mass and metastases, support the diagnosis of Cushing's syndrome due to an ectopic ACTH-producing tumor, as confirmed by immunohistochemical staining positive for ACTH in tumor cells

rejected.label: Parotid gland carcinoma
rejected.why: While the patient has a parotid gland mass, this diagnosis alone does not explain the hormonal imbalances and systemic symptoms

rejected.why: This is essentially synonymous with the champion diagnosis and does not provide additional distinct information

rejected.label: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence provided that points to this particular type of salivary gland tumor as the cause of the patient's symptoms

rejected.label: Adenoid cystic carcinoma
